lines.trans: Sit down, Clara! You ran half the city this morning; have a coffee.
Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.
Careful with that corner chair; wait ten seconds while I tighten this screw.

words.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

lines.trans: Done already? You carry a screwdriver everywhere, Mateo!
Old houses loosen one screw every Tuesday. Now you can sit down.
Look, you survived the breakfast rush and the mystery phone call!
Honestly, I feel much more at home here than in my old grey office.
Wait until Friday at noon! I want a front-row seat when the suitcase man walks in!
Nobody stares at guests. We hand over the suitcase and mind our own business.
Listen to him! Mateo is twice as curious as we are!
I am simply watching security. That is my job.

lines.trans: Sure, Mateo, your secret is safe with us!
See you soon!

meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

meanings.note: Opposite of apretar (to tighten).

examples.trans: I loosen the screw carefully.

examples.text: El mecánico aflojó la tuerca vieja.
examples.trans: The mechanic loosened the old nut.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition a + masculine article el; al + infinitive means 'upon doing'.

examples.text: Vamos al mercado por la mañana.
examples.trans: We go to the market in the morning.

examples.text: Al abrir la puerta, sonó el timbre.
examples.trans: Upon opening the door, the bell rang.

meanings.note: Placed after a noun, means 'historic' or 'old-fashioned'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.

examples.text: Encantada, Tomás, ¡siempre que nadie hable de vender pianos antiguos!
examples.trans: Gladly, Tomas, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: aprieto).

examples.text: Aprieto bien el tapón del termo.
examples.trans: I tighten the thermos cap firmly.

examples.text: Apretó el botón del timbre dos veces.
examples.trans: He pressed the doorbell button twice.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Commonly masculine (sin azúcar = without sugar).

examples.text: El azúcar es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The sugar is very important here.
We talk about the sugar.

meanings.note: Invariable before masculine or feminine singular nouns (cada día, cada mañana).

examples.trans: I open the cafe every morning.
Each room has its own key.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ending in -dad.

examples.trans: The city is here.

examples.text: Vemos las ciudades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cities from the door.

meanings.note: Alto y claro = loud and clear; ¡Claro! / ¡Pues claro! = Of course!

examples.text: El mensaje es alto y claro.
examples.trans: The message is loud and clear.
Well of course you can come in!

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Entrar/salir corriendo = to run in / run out.

examples.text: Corro para no perder el tren.
examples.trans: I run so I do not miss the train.

examples.text: Los niños corrieron hacia la fuente.
examples.trans: The children ran toward the fountain.

meanings.note: Unaccented in statements and time clauses (interrogative: cuándo).

examples.trans: Let me know when the taxi arrives.

examples.text: Cuando llueve, huele a tierra mojada.
examples.trans: When it rains, it smells like wet earth.

meanings.note: Con cuidado = carefully; ¡Cuidado con...! = Mind the...!

examples.text: El cuidado es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The care is very important here.
We talk about the care.

meanings.note: Por curiosidad = out of curiosity.

examples.text: La curiosidad es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The curiosity is very important here.
We talk about the curiosity.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Con desayuno incluido = with breakfast included.

examples.trans: The breakfast is here.

examples.text: Vemos los desayunos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the breakfasts from the door.

meanings.note: Built from des- + tornillo (screw).

examples.trans: The screwdriver is here.

examples.text: Vemos los destornilladores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screwdrivers from the door.

meanings.note: Diez sobre diez = ten out of ten.

examples.trans: There are ten minutes left before starting.
Your front desk deserves a ten.

meanings.note: El doble de... means 'double the amount of...'.

examples.trans: The double is here.

examples.text: Vemos los dobles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the doubles from the door.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Expresses location inside or on top of a surface (en la mesa = on the table).

examples.text: Las tazas están en la mesa.
examples.trans: The cups are on the table.

examples.text: Vivimos en Valencia todo el año.
examples.trans: We live in Valencia all year.

meanings.note: Said on introduction or when gladly accepting an invitation (encantado / encantada).

examples.trans: It is a delighted piece.

examples.text: ¡Encantada! Con leche y un poco de azúcar, por favor.
examples.trans: Gladly! With milk and a little sugar, please.

meanings.note: Places something between two people or things.

examples.text: La mesita está entre las dos sillas.
examples.trans: The small table is between the two chairs.
Among all of us we tidied the courtyard.

meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells g -> gu: entregué.

examples.trans: I hand the parcel over at reception.

examples.text: El cartero entregó una carta urgente.
examples.trans: The postman delivered an urgent letter.

meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'to' before things (escucha el agua).

examples.text: Escucho los pájaros desde mi cama.
examples.trans: I listen to the birds from my bed.

examples.text: Escuchamos la lluvia sobre las tejas.
examples.trans: We listened to the rain on the tiles.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

esperar.gloss: to wait; to wait for; to hope

meanings.en: to wait; to wait for; to hope
meanings.note: Covers both 'wait (for)' and 'hope'.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, please.
We hope you rest very well.

esquina.gloss: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)

meanings.en: corner (outer street corner or cake corner)
meanings.note: Outer corner where two streets meet, or the crisp corner of a baking tray.

examples.trans: The corner is here.

examples.text: Vemos las esquinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the corners from the door.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Forms: este (m sg), esta (f sg), estos (m pl), estas (f pl).

examples.trans: This courtyard is very quiet.
This morning it is very sunny.

meanings.note: Por favor literally means 'as a favour'.

examples.trans: The favour is here.

examples.text: Vemos los favores desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the favours from the door.

meanings.note: Encargada fija = permanent manager.

examples.trans: It is a permanent piece.

examples.text: Nadie mira fijo a los clientes. Entregamos la maleta y a lo nuestro.
examples.trans: Nobody stares at guests. We hand over the suitcase and mind our own business.

meanings.note: Primera fila = front row.

examples.trans: The row is here.

examples.text: Vemos las filas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rows from the door.

meanings.note: Plural grises.

examples.trans: It is a grey piece.

examples.text: Dos pares de zapatos marrones de hombre y jerséis grises.
examples.trans: Two pairs of men's brown shoes and grey sweaters.

meanings.note: ¡Mucho gusto! = Pleased to meet you!; estar a gusto = to feel comfortable.

examples.text: El gusto es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The pleasure is very important here.
We talk about the pleasure.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Plural los hombres.

examples.trans: The man is here.

examples.text: Vemos los hombres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the men from the door.

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Used with feminine plural nouns and clock hours (las ocho).

examples.trans: The windows face the garden.
We have breakfast at eight.

meanings.note: Café con leche = white coffee.

examples.text: La leche es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The milk is very important here.
We talk about the milk.

meanings.note: Hacer una llamada = to make a phone call.

examples.trans: The phone call is here.

examples.text: Vemos las llamadas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the phone calls from the door.

llevar.gloss: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)

meanings.en: to carry; to wear; to take; to spend (time)
meanings.note: Versatile verb for carrying items, wearing clothes/glasses, or duration.

examples.text: Llevo dos tazas calientes al jardín.
examples.trans: I carry two hot cups to the garden.

examples.text: Hoy lleva un abrigo gris oscuro.
examples.trans: Today he is wearing a dark grey coat.

lo.gloss: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)

meanings.en: it / him (direct object); the (neuter before adj/que)
meanings.note: Direct object pronoun before verbs (lo veo), and neuter article in lo que ('what') or lo mejor ('the best').

examples.text: Ya lo veo encima del estante.
examples.trans: I see it now on the shelf.

examples.text: Lo mejor del patio es la calma.
examples.trans: The best part of the courtyard is the calm.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Hacer la maleta = to pack one's suitcase.

examples.trans: This blue suitcase is very heavy.

examples.text: Guardo las llaves en la maleta.
examples.trans: I keep the keys in the suitcase.

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el martes, los martes.

examples.trans: The Tuesday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los martes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Tuesdays from the door.

meanings.note: La mañana = the morning; mañana (without article) = tomorrow.

examples.text: Por la mañana servimos café caliente.
examples.trans: In the morning we serve hot coffee.
See you tomorrow at eight!

meanings.note: Media vuelta = half-turn (turn around); medio vaso = half a glass.

examples.trans: It is a half piece.

examples.text: Oh, qué amable es usted, señor. Solo medio vaso.
examples.trans: Oh, how kind you are, sir. Just half a glass.

meanings.note: Al mediodía = at noon.

examples.text: El mediodía es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The noon is very important here.
We talk about the noon.

meanings.note: Plural mis (mi llave / mis llaves); unaccented, distinct from pronoun mí.

examples.trans: My suitcase is navy blue.

examples.text: Mis apuntes están en el bolsillo.
examples.trans: My notes are in my pocket.

meanings.note: Links two simultaneous actions.

examples.text: Espera aquí mientras abro la puerta.
examples.trans: Wait here while I open the door.

examples.text: Preparo el té mientras sale el pan.
examples.trans: I make the tea while the bread comes out.

mirar.gloss: to look; to look at; to watch

meanings.en: to look; to look at; to watch
meanings.note: Needs no preposition for 'at' (mira el reloj = look at the clock).

examples.text: Mira qué sol hace esta mañana.
examples.trans: Look how sunny it is this morning.

examples.text: Miramos el mapa antes de salir.
examples.trans: We look at the map before going out.

meanings.note: Describes a mystery caller or note.

examples.trans: It is a mysterious piece.

examples.text: Pues claro que vine. ¿Por qué te escondiste detrás de una nota misteriosa?
examples.trans: Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?
It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Feminine all-female plural: nosotras.

examples.text: Nosotros abrimos la posada a las siete.
examples.trans: We open the guesthouse at seven.

examples.text: Siéntese a tomar té con nosotros.
examples.trans: Sit down and have tea with us.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

meanings.note: Workplace or municipal desk.

examples.trans: The office is here.

examples.text: Vemos las oficinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the offices from the door.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la mejor parte.

examples.trans: The part is here.

examples.text: Vemos las partes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the parts from the door.

meanings.note: Un poco de mantequilla = a little butter.

examples.text: ¿Quiere un poco de miel en el té?
examples.trans: Would you like a little honey in your tea?

examples.text: Quedan pocos minutos para el mediodía.
examples.trans: Few minutes remain until noon.

poder.gloss: can; to be able to; may

meanings.en: can; to be able to; may
meanings.note: Irregular: puedo, pude, podría.

examples.trans: May I look at the tag again?

examples.text: Hoy podemos desayunar en el patio.
examples.trans: Today we can have breakfast in the courtyard.

por.gloss: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)

meanings.en: through; along; by; because of; in (time of day)
meanings.note: Por la mañana = in the morning; por favor = please; gracias por = thanks for.

examples.trans: We stroll through the old quarter.

examples.text: Por la mañana entra mucho sol.
examples.trans: In the morning plenty of sun comes in.

meanings.note: Shortens to primer before masculine singular nouns (el primer día); also used as adverb ('first').

examples.text: Hoy es mi primer día de trabajo.
examples.trans: Today is my first day of work.
The first room is vacant.

meanings.note: Tener prisa = be in a rush; ¡Date prisa! = Hurry up!

examples.trans: The hurry is here.

examples.text: Vemos las prisas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the hurrys from the door.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

meanings.note: Core connector and relative pronoun (unaccented, distinct from interrogative qué).

examples.trans: I hope that you rest very well.

examples.text: El pan de esta panadería huele genial.
examples.trans: The bread that The baker bakes smells great.

meanings.note: Sin querer = by accident; querer decir = to mean.

examples.trans: Would you like coffee or hot tea?
I opened it by accident.

meanings.note: Estar a salvo = to be safe; sano y salvo = safe and sound.

examples.trans: It is a safe piece.

examples.text: Ahí mismo, en la frente, sanas y salvas.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

meanings.note: As a masculine noun (el secreto), means 'secret'.

examples.trans: It is a secret piece.

examples.text: Claro, Mateo, ¡tu secreto está a salvo con nosotras!
examples.trans: Sure, Mateo, your secret is safe with us!

meanings.note: Also a masculine noun (un segundo = one second).

examples.trans: It is a second piece.

examples.text: Segunda: Te he echado de menos estos tres años.
examples.trans: Second: I missed you these three years.

meanings.note: Con seguridad = safely / for sure.

examples.trans: The safety is here.

examples.text: Vemos las seguridades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the safetys from the door.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (e -> ie: me siento, ¡siéntese!).

examples.text: Siéntese junto a la ventana, por favor.
examples.trans: Sit down by the window, please.
We sit down under the lemon tree.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

meanings.note: Wooden or folding chair.

examples.trans: The chair is here.

examples.text: Vemos las sillas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the chairs from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ir verb; sobrevivir a algo = survive something.

examples.text: Este olivo sobrevivió a muchas heladas.
examples.trans: This olive tree survived many frosts.

examples.text: Mis tazas favoritas sobrevivieron al viaje.
examples.trans: My favourite cups survived the trip.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

tener.gloss: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)

meanings.en: to have; to have to (tener que + inf)
meanings.note: Used in idioms: tener hambre/frío/miedo/prisa/razón; tener que = must.

examples.trans: We have eight quiet rooms.

examples.text: Tengo que cerrar la ventana ahora.
examples.trans: I have to close the window now.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?
Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Apretar un tornillo = tighten a screw.

examples.trans: The screw is here.

examples.text: Vemos los tornillos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the screws from the door.

meanings.note: Ir al trabajo = go to work.

examples.trans: The work is here.

examples.text: Vemos los trabajos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the works from the door.

meanings.note: Unaccented possessive (tu llave / tus llaves), distinct from accented pronoun tú.

examples.trans: Where is your toolbox?
I recognized your handwriting right away.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Invariable in plural: el viernes ('on Friday'), los viernes ('on Fridays').

examples.trans: The Friday is here.

examples.text: Vemos los viernes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the Fridays from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: El vecino vigila que la caldera funcione bien.
examples.trans: El vecino watches to make sure the boiler runs properly.

examples.text: Vigilamos la maleta hasta el mediodía.
examples.trans: We guarded the suitcase until noon.

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!

meanings.note: Often omitted in Spanish unless adding contrast or emphasis.

examples.text: Yo abro la puerta y tú llevas la linterna.
examples.trans: I will open the door and you carry the flashlight.
It is me, please open up.
